text:
Nashville arrives off a 5-2 win over STL five days ago that snapped a three-game winless run (0-1-2). Boston is two days removed from a 3-2 overtime loss at DAL that ended its five-game winning streak, though the Bruins still have points in six straight and are 4-0-1 in their last five.

The Bruins' results are running ahead of their play. They sit at a +14 goal difference on -1.4 expected, which means the quality of chances has been about even, with finishing and goaltending doing the lifting. At five on five, NSH has taken 45% of the expected goals in its games to BOS's 51%. Boston's penalty kill has been the weaker of the two special teams units, and the Bruins take 4.6 penalties a game. In net, projected starter Juuse Saros (NSH) is +1.5 goals saved above expected (how many goals he's stopped beyond what the shots should have produced) in 7 games, but was -10.2 last season. Michael DiPietro (BOS), projected to start over Jeremy Swayman, is +1.3 in two games.

Worth watching: Steven Stamkos (NSH) at 37% to score and David Pastrnak (BOS) at 32%, both top power play options. Matthew Poitras has 6 points in his last seven for BOS, and his chances back it up. Ice Sheet's under-the-radar pick is Adam Edstrom (NSH), a third-liner whose shots have been dangerous lately: 3.0 expected goals in his last 8 games, 19% to score.
